**Finding submitted: `missing` (medium severity) — TRANSITION**

**What I found.** The Agreement contains no post-termination transition assistance or data-return provision. Article XXI (p0138, "Effect of Termination") is entirely one-directional: our licence terminates automatically, we must ship back all Licensed Technology, API documentation and Confidential Information within five days and have an officer certify compliance, and "[a]ll of the Licensor's rights under this Agreement shall survive termination." I also checked the confidentiality article (p0124 — binds Licensee only), the insolvency/change-of-control termination triggers (p0132–p0137), the non-exclusive remedy article (p0142), and searched the full document for data/export/deletion language. Nothing obliges Licensor to return our hosted market data, order and trade records, to help us migrate, or to delete our data afterwards — a material gap in a hosted FX trading platform arrangement.

**Redline (validated, ok:true).** Inserted a new Article XXI-A after p0138 tracking the playbook's preferred position: (a) up to six months of transition assistance at Licensor's then-current rates on our request; (b) return of Licensee Data in a commonly used, machine-readable format within 30 days; (c) deletion thereafter with written certification. Because the Agreement has no "Customer Data" equivalent defined term, I defined "Licensee Data" inline to cover our and our customers' trade, order and transaction records hosted or processed by Licensor.

**Negotiation posture.** The comment flags the 90-day fallback (with the same 30-day export) if Licensor resists a six-month assistance window. Note the walk-away risk is live here: with no provision at all, Licensor could take the position it may delete our records immediately on termination, which is problematic given FX trade-record retention expectations.
